tier_reason: Lowered C to D: the only evidence is the README sentence 'twice as fast as libpng' with no measurement (lodepng_benchmark.cpp times lodepng alone and never links libpng), and the enricher's code reading shows the final commit 61f9f24 broke correctness: bytewidth = bpp/8 means 1-, 2- and 4-bit grey and palette PNGs are never unfiltered (depng has no case 0) and decode to zeros or garbage; an Adam7 image with width or height of 4 or less gives depng h = 0 and the do-while wraps about 4 billion rows (out-of-bounds read and write); the encoder passes a NULL output buffer to libdeflate_zlib_compress; two libdeflate objects leak per state; invalid filter bytes are not rejected. The README's MMX, AVX2, NEON and 'TurboPNG API' claims match nothing in the tree (SSE2 only).

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 'twice as fast as libpng' on x86, x86-64 or ARM; no measurement, harness or baseline build exists in the repository (lodepng_benchmark.cpp never links libpng).
corrections.caveats: Directional claim only. Correctness bugs at HEAD (code reading, not run): sub-8-bit grey and palette PNGs are never unfiltered after commit 61f9f24 (bytewidth = bpp/8, no case 0 in depng); Adam7 images with a dimension of 4 or less wrap the row loop (out-of-bounds read and write); the encoder passes a NULL output buffer to libdeflate_zlib_compress; two libdeflate objects leak per state; invalid filter bytes are not rejected. README SIMD and API claims match nothing in the tree (SSE2 only); the Linux Makefile hard-codes libdeflatestatic.lib.

tier_reason: Lowered C to D: the README's '3x AVX2 / 2x SSE' line dates from the February 2017 kernel e67dffa (6-bit weights, up to 3 levels off OpenCV, 57.4% of colours differing) and was never re-measured after the 30 September 2018 Q15 rewrite; the SSE path was removed (issue #5), so the 2x figure has no code behind it, and the only public run (issue #1, a Debug build) shows OpenCV 3.4.3 at 2592.71 us against RGB2Y at 15139.5 us. corrections.claimed_speedup: README (dating from the February 2017 kernel, never re-measured after the 2018 Q15 rewrite): 'roughly 3x faster than OpenCV with AVX2, 2x with SSE only'; the SSE path no longer exists. The only public run (issue #1, Debug build) has OpenCV 3.4.3 at 2592.71 us versus RGB2Y 15139.5 us.
corrections.caveats: No measured number for the current code. Exhaustive check of all 16,777,216 BGR triples against OpenCV 4.x: 33.2% of outputs differ by 1 (max 1). The multithreaded row split overruns the destination at 18 or more threads (385 rows on 24 threads, 721 or 1000 on 64); the tail over-reads 1-28 bytes; stride is in pixels with packed output while the reference writes strided; __forceinline and an unannotated fallthrough break the g++ -Werror Makefile; the function is really BGR2Y (issue #4).

tier_reason: Lowered A to C under the rule that numbers measured on code later fixed for a correctness bug go to C: the QOIR run (November 2022) timed the fast_lossless encoder at effort 1 whose palette detection checked 8 pixels then inserted, missing hash collisions and producing lossy output from a lossless encode on RGBA few-colour images (issue #4287); the pattern is present from v0.7.0 (July 2022) through v0.11.1 and was fixed in PR #4291 (June 2025). QOIR never round-trip checks, so the 0.2171 compression ratio may be slightly flattered; encode speed is probably unaffected, but the measured code was not a correct lossless encoder on part of the corpus. The WangXuan95 shootout timing also includes cjxl.exe process start against in-process Pillow.

corrections.caveats: Measured on code later fixed for a correctness bug: the 2022 fast_lossless effort-1 palette detection could emit lossy output on RGBA few-colour images (issue #4287, fixed PR #4291 in June 2025), and QOIR does no round-trip check, so the 0.2171 ratio may be slightly flattered. Different format: FJXL writes JPEG XL, so readers need a JPEG XL decoder, and libjxl decodes at 33.16 MP/s against libpng 56.18 and WebP lossless 89.94 in the same run; files are about 10% smaller than libpng's but about 31% larger than WebP lossless. Default CMake disables the fjxl AVX-512 path; x86 SIMD is gated on !_MSC_VER so MSVC and clang-cl builds are probably scalar; the fast path falls back on animation, crop and extra channels. The WangXuan95 timing includes cjxl.exe process start.
